target_customer: Robotics and physical-AI labs buying dexterous hands and data-collection gloves; later factories and logistics operators
problem: Robot manipulation lacks data and hardware that match human hand dexterity (embodiment gap).
business_model: Hardware sales (robot hand, gloves) to fund data collection and a manipulation model; later automation sales
product_category: Dexterous robot hands and robot-learning data gloves

founders.name: Ryan Xie
founders.background_notes: Described by YC as a serial hardware founder; Daniel's brother per the launch post.

technical_complexity.rationale: High degree-of-freedom direct-drive hand with matched glove and a learning pipeline combines mechatronics and robot-learning research.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware is replicable by well-funded robotics firms; the data flywheel is planned, not shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early; no incumbent action found.

market_need_then: Physical-AI labs need dexterous hardware and demonstration data; the company claims early hand sales including Amazon (launch post, unverified).

identity.voice_and_tone: Short declarative copy: Designed. Built. Refined. Bring Human Dexterity to Robots.

brand_strength.rationale: Too early and no sourced evidence on brand impact.

outcome_analysis: Origami Robotics is a W26 company with a five-person team selling a dexterous robot hand and data-collection glove, with a plan to move from hardware sales to data collection and a general manipulation model. Funding is unverified, with conflicting reports of $500K and $12.5M, and no outcome exists yet, so the record is a snapshot of a very early company.
notes: Funding not recorded: Caplight and robotics.press list $500K seed (Mar 2026), a pages.dev hiring page claims $12.5M seed; none is a primary source.
